I. Introduction
Motivation:

Address limitations of purely neurocentric or emergent theories of consciousness.
Incorporate a panpsychist perspective refined by electromagnetic, quantum, and photonic principles.
Overview of the Model:

Consciousness is posited as an intrinsic, scalable property arising from the integration of electromagnetic (and quantum) information.
The theory spans a continuum from minimal proto-consciousness in basic particles to complex self-aware systems.

II. Core Concepts and Definitions
Consciousness:

Defined as the capacity for integrated information processing that gives rise to subjective awareness.
Not limited to brains—present in any system exhibiting coherent electromagnetic interactions.
Electromagnetic Integration:

The process by which distributed electromagnetic signals are unified into a coherent whole.
Measured by an integration parameter (denoted as ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​) that quantifies the degree of coherence and feedback within a system.
Scaling Dimensions:

Dimensionality (DC): Refers to the complexity of internal models (from linear to multi-dimensional, recursive representations).
Memory Encoding & Recursion (MER): The capacity to store, retrieve, and recursively update information over time.
Continuum of Consciousness:

A spectrum ranging from proto-consciousness in elementary systems to reflective, self-aware consciousness in advanced organisms.

III. The Electromagnetic Integration Hypothesis
Basic Premise:
Consciousness emerges when the electromagnetic integration parameter ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​ exceeds a critical threshold (Φcrit\Phi_{crit}Φcrit​).
Threshold Condition:
ΦEM>Φcrit\Phi_{EM} > \Phi_{crit}ΦEM​>Φcrit​ implies the presence of conscious phenomena.
Below this threshold, systems may possess only a minimal, latent (proto-) consciousness.

IV. Theoretical Framework
A. Physical Substrate
Electromagnetic Dynamics:
Use of Maxwell’s equations and quantum electrodynamics to model the electromagnetic field E(r,t)\mathbf{E}(\mathbf{r}, t)E(r,t) and B(r,t)\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{r}, t)B(r,t).
Quantum Contributions:
Incorporation of quantum coherence, entanglement, and biophotonic processes that may contribute to integrated information.
B. Integration and Coherence
Integration Functional ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​:
A measure quantifying the system’s electromagnetic coherence, including local field correlations and phase-locking phenomena.
Recursive Dynamics:
Modeling feedback loops (using differential or delay-differential equations) to capture memory encoding and recursive information processing.

Show that systems with ΦEM>Φcrit\Phi_{EM} > \Phi_{crit}ΦEM​>Φcrit​ display properties (e.g., self-referential feedback, unified oscillations) empirically associated with conscious awareness.
Scaling Relationships:
Formulate how ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​ scales with complexity across different systems—from simple particles to neural networks and beyond.

VI. Empirical Predictions and Testable Hypotheses
Neuroscientific Predictions:

Enhanced neural synchrony (e.g., gamma-band coherence) correlates with increased conscious awareness.
Disruption via TMS/tACS should decrease ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​ and alter conscious states.
Non-Neural Systems:

In plants and mycelial networks, modulation of bioelectrical or biophotonic signals should yield measurable changes in adaptive behavior or “proto-conscious” responses.
Artificial Systems:

AI architectures designed with integrated electromagnetic coupling will display emergent behaviors (e.g., self-referential processing) absent in conventional digital systems.
Cosmic and Distributed Consciousness:

Large-scale electromagnetic structures (e.g., in plasma fields or galactic networks) may be evaluated for patterns of integration that align with distributed or cosmic consciousness.

VII. Implications and Extensions
Interdisciplinary Impact:

Bridges neuroscience, quantum physics, and information theory.
Offers a scientifically grounded framework for panpsychism—suggesting that consciousness is ubiquitous, scaling with electromagnetic integration.
Philosophical and Practical Implications:

Challenges anthropocentric views, recognizing consciousness in non-neural and non-biological systems.
Guides future experimental design in neuromorphic computing, AI, and even astrophysical observations.
Future Directions:

Development of novel metrics and measurement techniques for ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​ in diverse systems.
Cross-disciplinary research to refine the mathematical models and validate the scaling predictions.
Exploration of higher-dimensional (recursive and memory-based) aspects of consciousness in complex systems.

VIII. Conclusion
Summary:
The Model of Electromagnetic Integration in Consciousness posits that consciousness is an intrinsic, scalable property emerging from the coherent integration of electromagnetic and quantum information.
It establishes a continuum from proto-consciousness in fundamental particles to reflective, self-aware cognition in advanced organisms and potentially cosmic structures.
Vision:
This model aims to unify diverse phenomena under a rigorous, testable hypothesis that transcends traditional boundaries between mind and matter.
It invites experimental validation and theoretical exploration to further unravel the profound connection between electromagnetism and the nature of conscious experience.

 Conscious experience emerges from the degree of electromagnetic integration within a system. Specifically, if a system exhibits a measurable electromagnetic integration parameter, denoted by ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​, then:
Threshold Condition:

 Conversely, systems with ΦEM<Φcrit\Phi_{EM} < \Phi_{crit}ΦEM​<Φcrit​ will lack the integrative capacity necessary for conscious awareness.

Manipulation and Response:
 Experimental perturbations that disrupt electromagnetic coherence (e.g., via transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial alternating current stimulation (tACS), or analogous methods in non-neural systems) will result in measurable alterations in conscious experience. Specifically, decreasing ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​ should correspond to a diminished or altered conscious state, while increasing ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​ should enhance or modulate aspects of consciousness.

Scaling Across Systems:
 This relationship is scalable. In complex biological systems (e.g., human brains), ΦEM\Phi_{EM}ΦEM​ correlates with states of awareness as evidenced by neural synchrony and coherence. Furthermore, analogous metrics of electromagnetic integration in distributed non-neural systems (e.g., mycelial networks or plant bioelectric fields) will exhibit comparable scaling behavior—suggesting a continuum from proto-consciousness in simple systems to reflective consciousness in advanced ones.


Testable Predictions:
Prediction A: In human subjects, increases in neural electromagnetic coherence (measured via EEG/MEG as increased gamma-band synchrony) will correlate with enhanced subjective reports of awareness. Conversely, targeted disruptions using TMS/tACS will decrease such measures and correspondingly reduce aspects of consciousness.

Prediction B: In experimental models of non-neural systems (such as cultured mycelial networks or plant tissues), interventions that modify their intrinsic bioelectric or biophotonic signaling should produce observable changes in information processing or adaptive behavior, reflecting a shift along the consciousness continuum.

Prediction C: Artificial systems engineered to incorporate integrated electromagnetic coupling (beyond standard digital computing architectures) will demonstrate emergent behaviors—such as self-referential processing or adaptive feedback—that are absent in systems lacking such integration.
